## Summary

The audit runner's code-quality scan is documented to lint only the work item's changed files (`SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` AC1: "the code-quality scan runs only over the git changed-file list … not the full repo"), but it silently falls back to a **whole-repo** scan whenever the changed-file list is empty. For an item whose work is already committed to `dev` (the normal post-merge state, and the state the merge gate integrates to), `git diff --name-only HEAD` + `git status --porcelain` are both empty, so `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files or None)` receives `None` and lints the entire repository. Any pre-existing critical/high ruff finding in an unrelated file then blocks Phase 1 of every audit in that repo — a recurrence of the defect class fixed by `SA-0MSG83Z4Z004YH2P` ("EXE001 misclassified as 'high' severity blocks audits on unrelated files") and a contradiction of `SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` AC1.

## Repro

1. Work item `LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS` (llm) is merged to `origin/dev`; the local checkout is clean at the delivered commit `66ddbe93`.
2. `git diff --name-only HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` are both empty.
3. Run `audit_runner.py issue LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS --force`: `_git_changed_files` returns `[]`, so `run_code_quality(files=None)` scans the whole repo.
4. The whole-repo scan returns 4 findings, all outside the item's change set:
   - `ruff F841` (critical) `proxy/tests/test_watchdog_upstream_cancellation.py:197,277`
   - `ruff I001` (medium) `proxy/tests/test_compaction_summarizer.py:594`, `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py:503`
5. Phase 1 blocks on the critical findings; every AC is demoted `met → partial` and Phase 2 is skipped; `Ready to close: No`.

Verified directly: `run_code_quality(project_root=<llm>, files=[the item's 4 changed files])` returns **0 findings** — the item's own work is lint-clean.

## Impact (observed)

- The audit of `LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS` (2026-09-26) produced a spurious `Ready to close: No` from findings belonging to other work items. The item was only accepted because the Phase 1 false-positive screen *also* degraded (provider error / concurrency limit), leaving the run fallback-tainted and the lifecycle restored to `completed`/`in_review`.
- Had the screen succeeded, the `F841` findings would have been classified `genuine` and the unrelated item would have been **demoted** `in_review → open`.
- The findings already have tracking items (quality epics): `LP-0MUHSWSI8004AFU4`, `LP-0MUHSWS8M001QY46`, `LP-0MUHVMLGB0056C0K`.

## Suggested fix

- When the git changed-file list is empty, scope the code-quality scan to the item's **Key Files** and/or its committed diff (the commits the merge gate resolved, e.g. `git diff-tree -r --name-only <commit>^..<commit>`), instead of falling back to the whole repo.
- An empty effective scope should lint nothing (skip with a documented reason), never the entire repository.
- Cover the already-merged / clean-checkout case in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. For an item whose work is already committed and whose checkout is clean, the audit code-quality scan lints only the item's files (Key Files and/or its delivered commits), never the whole repo.
2. An empty effective scope lints nothing (documented skip), rather than scanning the whole repository.
3. Unit tests cover the empty-changed-file case and assert `run_code_quality` is not invoked with `files=None` (whole repo) for an already-merged item.
4. Re-auditing an item in a repo containing unrelated critical ruff findings no longer reports those findings against that item.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSG83Z4Z004YH2P` — EXE001 misclassified as 'high' severity blocks audits on unrelated files (completed) — same defect class.
- `SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` — Audit: scope code-quality scan to changed files, read-only (completed) — introduced the scoping this bug regresses in the empty-diff case.
- Discovered during the audit of `LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS` (llm).

data.description:
`wl sync` overwrites a locally-persisted audit result with an older copy, silently reverting a just-written audit (data loss / audit-record corruption).

## Problem

When a `wl sync` runs after a local audit has been persisted (via the canonical audit persister / `wl audit-set`), the locally written audit text is replaced by an older copy of the audit. The item's other fields (status, stage, `needsProducerReview`, comments, description) are preserved, so the store is left internally inconsistent: the lifecycle reflects the new verdict while the stored audit shows a stale verdict.

Observed 2026-09-26 on `LP-0MSPZUD4G007IYGH` in the LLM project (`/home/rgardler/projects/llm`):

1. The audit runner persisted a new `Ready to close: No` audit at `2026-09-26T13:34:32.382Z`; `wl audit-show` read it back immediately (verified).
2. A herdr-scheduled `wl sync` ran (`.worklog/last-sync-time` advanced to `2026-09-26T13:38:00Z`); afterwards `wl audit-show` returned the **old** `2026-08-15T12:59:45.425Z` `Ready to close: Yes` audit.
3. Re-persisted via `persist_audit.py` at `2026-09-26T13:37:27.757Z`; a further `wl sync` reverted it again.
4. Re-persisted once more at `2026-09-26T13:39:21.882Z` (no sync running); it remained stable while no sync ran.

The item's status/stage (`open`/`plan_complete`) and its comments (including ones added after the new audit) survived each sync — only the audit text reverted.

## Evidence

- The synced export `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` contains only `workitem` and `comment` records — **no audit field/record at all** (`grep -c '<new-fingerprint>' worklog-data.jsonl` → 0; the `workitem` record keys do not include `audit`).
- Therefore the audit cannot be propagating through the git sync export, yet the old audit reappears after sync — suggesting the audit is not carried by the export and the sync restores/keeps an older audit from another source, or the merge drops local-only audit changes.
- Commands used: `wl audit-show <id> --json`, `persist_audit.py --issue-id <id> --file <report>`, `git for-each-ref refs/worklog/...`, `.worklog/last-sync-time`.
- Worklog prefix: `SA` (this repo). The affected store was `LP` (LLM project).

## Impact

- Audits persisted by the canonical audit runner can be silently reverted, leaving `status`/`stage` inconsistent with the stored audit text (e.g. item demoted to `open`/`plan_complete` while `audit-show` reports a stale `Yes`).
- Operators and orchestrators reading `wl audit-show` can be misled about whether an item is ready to close.
- Concurrent syncs (herdr-scheduled) make the loss deterministic during busy periods, so re-persisting does not reliably fix it.

## Expected behaviour

- A `wl sync` must never downgrade a newer locally-persisted audit to an older one. Merge semantics for audit text should be last-write-wins by audit time (or audits should be excluded from sync-triggered overwrites until pushed).
- If the sync cannot carry audit text in the git export, it must leave the local audit untouched rather than reverting it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Reproduce in a test: persist audit A (older), then a newer audit B on the same item, run the sync/merge path, and assert `wl audit-show` returns B (not A).
2. The synced worklog export either carries audit records/fields, or the sync merge explicitly preserves the newest local audit (documented decision).
3. A sync that cannot represent audits leaves the local audit unchanged (no revert).
4. Regression fixture uses two audits with distinct `auditedAt` timestamps and the real sync export/import path.
5. Existing worklog sync tests pass.

## Notes

- Discovered during the audit of `LP-0MSPZUD4G007IYGH` (proxy usage analysis fast/cheap bucketing). Recording it here as instructed by the operator; out of scope for that audit.
- Related: audit persistence ordering contract (comments before persistence), and the audit freshness gate — a reverted audit text also makes the content-fingerprint freshness gate evaluate against the wrong (older) report.
data.title: wl sync reverts locally-persisted audit results to a stale older audit

# Repair wl sync for the operator's GitHub-identity checkout

`discovered-from:SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1` (created during that item's session; actioned by operator directive).

## Problem statement

`wl sync` in this checkout cannot merge incoming worklog data: the author-identity
gate (SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX) refuses all remote `refs/worklog/data` commits because
they are authored by `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com` (the operator's
GitHub identity) while the local checkout's `user.email` is `pi@local`. Additional
blockers are 31 incident-era commits from the leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident
(2026-09-26) authored as `t@t.com` — a hardcoded `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` sentinel
that must NOT be whitelisted.

## Existing state

- `.worklog/config.yaml` previously had no `syncAllowedAuthors` — the gate had
  only the strict user.email comparison.
- `refs/worklog/data` history contains 31 contiguous `t@t.com` commits
  (positions `345ea154a..fbf0b5bda`, 2026-09-26) that the gate must keep refusing.
- `wl sync` therefore could not merge or push (`1559 incoming commit(s) fail the
  author-identity gate`; after whitelisting the operator identity: `31`).

## Desired change

1. Add the operator's GitHub noreply email to `syncAllowedAuthors` in
   `.worklog/config.yaml` so legitimate operator-identity commits pass the gate.
2. Purge the 31 incident-era `t@t.com` commits from `refs/worklog/data` history
   (re-parent past the block without changing any tree content), so the gate has
   nothing to refuse.
3. `wl sync` completes and pushes the current SQLite store (incl. SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** `wl sync --dry-run` no longer refuses on author identity.
2. **AC2:** `wl sync` completes successfully (merge + push), and
   `SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1` appears in `refs/worklog/data`.
3. **AC3:** No `t@t.com`-authored commits remain on `refs/worklog/data`.
4. **AC4:** `t@t.com` is NOT added to `syncAllowedAuthors` (sentinel emails stay
   refused — the quarantine is preserved).
5. **AC5:** The final `refs/worklog/data` tree is identical to the pre-purge tree
   (verified via `git diff`, plus work item count preserved).

## Key Files

- `.worklog/config.yaml` — `syncAllowedAuthors` allow-list entry.
- `refs/worklog/data` — incident-block purge (git history rewrite).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: force-push history rewrite on a shared branch.** Mitigation: the rewrite
  only re-parents the post-block linear history; trees are untouched; the loss of
  31 incident-erа commits is the intended quarantine. Any clone that fast-forwards
  is unaffected; others receive the rewritten chain on their next fetch.
- **Assumption:** `t@t.com` commits carry no legitimate post-incident data (they
  are in the 2026-09-26 incident window, superseded by the 2026-09-27+
  operator-identity snapshots).

Discovered-from:SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU.

## Summary

`wl sync` refuses to merge inbound worklog commits on refs/worklog/data: 4 commits (66b8e59b, a31dfb9a, 664d5b55, 1afacea2) authored `Sorra the Orc <pi@local>` (2026-10-15) fail the author gate — `pi@local` does not match configured `user.email` (`250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`) and is not in `syncAllowedAuthors`.

This blocks pushing the local close of SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU (and any other local worklog mutations) to origin. Local DB update succeeded; only remote sync is blocked.

## Verified state (2026-10-16 plan session)

- Exactly 4 gating commits, all `pi@local`, after last-synced-ref `9727585074`: `66b8e59b`, `a31dfb9a`, `664d5b55`, `1afacea2` (verified via `git log 97275850..refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data`).
- Gate semantics (worklog package `sync.js::checkAuthorIdentity`): a commit passes if author email matches `user.email` OR is in `syncAllowedAuthors`. Empty-email gate is never bypassed.
- 3 older `pi@local` commits (2026-09-16) predate last-synced-ref and are not gating.
- Main-checkout identity is healthy (`check_git_identity.py` → ok); the offending pushes came from a pi session with unset/incorrect identity.
- Stranded data is real: e.g. SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC (the earlier config fix) is absent from the local store.

## Decisions (operator, 2026-10-16)

- **Remediation of the 4 stranded commits:** one-time operator-authorized `wl sync --allow-foreign-author` (option a) — the designed escape hatch; no shared-history rewrite; the subsequent correctly-authored push advances last-synced-ref past the offenders.
- **Recurrence prevention:** add `pi@local` to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` for this project (operator-chosen option c), so pi-session-authored sync commits pass the gate. This deliberately widens the project gate to accept `pi@local` (empty-email gate still enforced); the general guard `scripts/check_git_identity.py` must NOT be hardened to flag `pi@local` (that would contradict the allow-list).

## Goal

Restore `wl sync` so local worklog mutations push to origin, and prevent recurrence of author-identity refusals for pi-session commits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** `wl sync` completes without an author-identity refusal, and previously-stranded items (e.g. SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC) are present in the local store; `last-synced-ref` advances past the 4 offending commits.
- [ ] **AC2** The one-time `--allow-foreign-author` remediation is operator-authorized and recorded in a comment with the exact command and output (safety-gate provenance).
- [ ] **AC3** `pi@local` is added to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` (project scope), and a regression test pins that the config allow-list accepts a `pi@local`-authored commit while an arbitrary foreign email is still refused.
- [ ] **AC4** Full test suite passes on a clean build; all changes committed with work-item association.

## Plan (approved 2026-10-16; 3 children, test-first)

1. **Author-gate incident regression tests** (test-first) — drive the gate/guard decision for the `pi@local` allow-list change; red before, green after.
2. **Recover stranded worklog data** (operator-authorized) — one-time `wl sync --allow-foreign-author`, verify stranded items present, last-synced-ref advances.
3. **Add `pi@local` to syncAllowedAuthors** (project allow-list) — `.worklog/config.yaml` change + docs note, depends on 1.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which remediation for the 4 stranded commits — (a) one-time authorized `wl sync --allow-foreign-author`, (b) rewrite the 4 authors and force-update refs/worklog/data, or (c) add `pi@local` to syncAllowedAuthors?" — Answer (operator, 2026-10-16): "(a)". Final: one-time authorized `--allow-foreign-author` merge; no history rewrite. Rationale: designed escape hatch, no shared-ref rewrite.
- Q: "Scope of recurrence prevention — (i) harden `check_git_identity.py` to flag `pi@local` + document, (ii) additionally enforce identity at pi-session/worktree setup, (iii) defer?" — Answer (operator, 2026-10-16): "Add pi@local to the allow list for this project". Final: option (c) from the remediation list — add `pi@local` to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml`; do NOT harden the guard. Note: this intentionally widens the gate for this project (empty-email gate still never bypassed).

Child of SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5 (Raise TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY 2->3 with mini-F7 validation). This is the **gating measurement** for the default raise.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want a recorded measurement of 8 real suite executions at ceiling 3 versus ceiling 2 on the 16-core host, so raising the default is an evidence-backed decision (mirroring the audit F7 calibration, SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Measurement runs **after** SA-0MVE98T1M006A17T lands (per-suite worker pools bounded); the work item records the blocker's completion evidence and host CPU count.
- `python3 skill/shared/validate_test_fanout.py --ceiling 2 --n 8 --out /tmp/ceiling-2.json` then the same with `--ceiling 3` are both executed on the 16-core host, with `--no-cache` paths only (no cache hits bypassing the semaphore).
- The baseline (1/5/15-min load and swap) is sampled immediately before each batch; results report the baseline **and** the batch-attributable peak deltas, never an absolute-load-only claim.
- Pass gate is evaluated and recorded: batch-attributable load delta < 4, no swap growth, and ceiling-3 drain time <= 1.10 x ceiling-2 drain time.
- Raw results are committed as `docs/dev/test-ceiling-validation.json` (precedent: `docs/dev/audit-ceiling-validation.json`) and reproduced as a results table in the work item, including both runs' `config`, baseline, peak load/process counts, swap before/after and drain times.
- If the pass gate fails, the item records the failure plus a recommended alternative (keep 2, or re-measure after remediation) and the dependent raise is left unstarted; no threshold is retro-fitted to a failing measurement without recording it.
- Reproduction commands are recorded verbatim in the work item so any maintainer can repeat the measurement.

- Parent AC2 traceability: mini-F7 measurement gates the change — pass gate is batch-attributable load delta < 4, no swap growth, and drain time at ceiling 3 <= 1.10 x the ceiling-2 drain; raw results are recorded in the work item (table) and as a committed JSON artifact (`docs/dev/test-ceiling-validation.json`).
## Minimal implementation

- Wait for the blocker child/edge to clear, confirm the host CPU count, then run the two documented invocations sequentially (not concurrently).
- Extract `batch.elapsed_seconds`, `batch.baseline_load`, `peak.load`, `before/after` swap, and `peak.processes` from each JSON.
- Compute the three gate metrics and state pass/fail explicitly.
- Commit the merged artifact (both runs) plus a table in the work item comment.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/test-ceiling-validation.json` (new artifact)
- `skill/shared/validate_test_fanout.py` (harness)
- `docs/dev/audit-ceiling-validation.json` (artifact format precedent)
- `docs/dev/fanout-batch-validation.json` (artifact format precedent)

## Dependencies

- SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5.2 (harness implementation).
- SA-0MVE98T1M006A17T (blocker: bounded per-suite worker pools) — measurement is not meaningful before it lands.

## Deliverables

- Committed measurement artifact and a recorded pass/fail verdict that gates SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5.4.

## Risks and assumptions

- Shared-host noise: mitigated by attributable deltas, a sampled baseline and a recorded host state; the gate never depends on absolute load.
- The synthetic payload models suite-level concurrency only; the artifact states this explicitly and pairs the result with the blocker's per-suite evidence.

```
- 4617ae25: author email 'pi@local' does not match configured user.email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com'
worklog: pre-push sync failed (pushing anyway)
```

The code push still lands (the hook continues with a warning), but the worklog
data branch on the remote is not advanced, so work-item/comment data stays
stale on the remote until a data commit with a matching author identity is
produced.

## Root cause (observed)

Worklog data commits on the shared `refs/worklog/data` branch may be authored
with the fallback identity `pi@local` (e.g. an agent host without
`git config user.email` set). `wl sync`'s merge gate rejects any incoming data
commit whose author email differs from the configured `user.email`, which is
correct for provenance but leaves the local store unable to merge.

## Desired outcome

Investigate and fix so legitimate local worklog data (created by `wl`) is not
silently stranded by an identity mismatch, e.g.:

- Set a repository/user git identity on every agent host that runs `wl sync`
  (document the requirement in the install script), and/or
- Make the author-identity gate report an actionable remediation and allow an
  explicit override for trusted local data commits.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reproducing with an incoming `pi@local` worklog commit yields an actionable
  error naming the fix (configure `user.email` or use the documented override).
- A documented, tested path lets an operator merge trusted local worklog data
  after verifying provenance (no silent bypass).
- Regression test covers a mismatched-author incoming data commit.
- Docs updated (install/sync reference).

# implement.py drive reports child as failed on session timeout even when the child's work completed and terminal state was reached

## Headline

`implement.py drive <parent-id>` treats a per-child session **timeout** (`subprocess.TimeoutExpired` in `_default_session_spawner`) as a hard child failure — it stops the whole epic chain and reports `success: false` / `failed_child` — **without reconciling against the child's actual work-item state**. Observed in the WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB epic (three children): each child session was killed at the per-child timeout (3600s/7200s/10800s) **after** the child had already committed and pushed to `dev`, yet `drive` reported:

```
"result": "failed",
"reason": "Child session for WL-0MVGU4S58003IRXV timed out after 3600s."
```

In two of the three cases the child had verifiably reached terminal state (status `completed`/stage `in_review` + commit on `origin/dev`); in the third the work was pushed but the final `StatusLifecycle` terminal update had not yet run, leaving the item stranded `in-progress` (manually finalised afterwards).

## Problem statement

`implement.py drive` (SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9) spawns a fresh Pi session per child via `_default_session_spawner`:

- `subprocess.run([pi, "-p", "/skill:implement <child>", "--approve", "--no-extensions"], cwd=worktree, timeout=child_timeout)`.
- On `TimeoutExpired` it returns `{"success": false, "reason": "Child session for <id> timed out after Ns"}`.
- `phase_drive` breaks on any `not spawn_result["success"]`, recording `"result": "failed"` and stopping.

The drive loop never re-queries the child with `wl show` after a timeout to check whether the child actually finished (`status: completed / stage: in_review`, commit on `dev`). `_is_terminal_child` exists and is used by `phase_parent`, but the drive loop decides success purely from the spawned process's exit code/exit-within-timeout, not from the work item's state.

**Observable outcomes (from WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB, implement session herdr-1792524101-1636143-211):**

1. Child work is complete + pushed + item already terminal, but the drive reports the child as failed and stops the chain → operator must manually re-inspect and re-run `parent`.
2. Child killed by the timeout **between push and the final `StatusLifecycle` terminal update** → item left `in-progress` with work on `dev` (an orphaned in-progress that `wl next` filters out); a human/agent must manually finalise the status.
3. No diagnostic distinguishes "completed-late" from "genuinely stuck" — the report only has the generic "timed out after Ns" reason.

## Users

- **herdr downtime dispatcher / producers** driving epics: needs `drive` to complete children reliably and report truthful per-child results.
- **Epic owner / auditor** reading `drive --json` output: a `failed` child that is actually `completed`/`in_review` on `dev` is a false negative; the audit trail is wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a driven child's session times out but the child's work item has reached a terminal state (status `completed`/`done` or stage `in_review`) with its commit pushed to `dev`, the drive report does **not** fail that child and does **not** stop the chain: it records the actual terminal status (e.g. result `ok`/`completed-late` with the terminal evidence), continues driving remaining children, and advances the parent when all children are terminal. Unit-testable with a fake spawner that simulates a timeout while `wl show` reports the child as terminal (like `phase_drive`'s existing injectable `spawn_session`/`parent_runner`).
- When a driven child's session times out and the child is **not** terminal, the existing hard-failure behaviour is preserved (report fails the child, stops the chain) — regression-guarded.
- A child whose work was pushed to `dev` but whose item is still `in-progress` after its session is killed (missing terminal update) is detected at the next `phase_parent`/`drive` pass and finalised to `completed`/`in_review` (or a clear diagnostic is emitted naming the stranded item) — the item must not remain an orphaned `in-progress` blocking `wl next`.
- The per-child `children_driven` entry or failure reason distinguishes "timed out but child completed" from "timed out, child incomplete" with the terminal evidence (status/stage/commit) so the report is truthful.
- Existing tests for `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` continue to pass; new tests cover the timeout-reconciliation paths (unit tests in the implement-skill test suite).

## Constraints

- Keep the session-per-child isolation and per-child worktree semantics unchanged (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9).
- The reconciliation must be read-only against `wl` (no mutation of a possibly-terminal child's state beyond the existing finalise path); do not re-spawn a session for an already-terminal child (existing "terminal children are never re-implemented" guard).
- Do not change the actual per-child timeout mechanism itself unless the RCA shows it is wrong (the defect is the *consequence handling*, not the timeout).

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `_default_session_spawner` (line ~5160) — timeout → `success: false`, generic reason.
  - `phase_drive` (line ~5295) — breaks on `not spawn_result["success"]`, no terminal-state reconciliation.
  - `_is_terminal_child` / `_is_terminal_status` (line ~740) — already used by `phase_parent`.
- `examples/` and implement-skill tests cover drive loop, parent advancement, worktree-placement guard; none cover timeout-with-terminal-child reconciliation (per repo search).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive`, `_default_session_spawner`, terminal-state helpers.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — extend drive-loop tests with a timeout-reconciliation fixture (injectable `spawn_session`).

## Related work

- SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9 (completed) — implement skill: drive all epic children to completion (fresh session per child).
- SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52 (completed) — when implementing an epic, start a new session for each child.
- SA-0MUY9PYBD009Y7J5 (completed) — fix Pi turn_end boundary error in driven child sessions (child stderr noise; related child-session reliability).
- WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB (ContextHub epic) — the epic whose three driven children exhibited this in production.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption A1.** The observed real-world outcomes (false-negative failed report + stranded `in-progress`) are caused by the missing terminal-state reconciliation in `phase_drive` (the only code path consistent with "work pushed + item terminal, yet drive reports timeout failure"). This is the same defect class as the manual finalisation needed for WL-0MVGUA9EY003XFAD.
- **Assumption A2.** A reconciliation pass is preferable to raising the timeout: child sessions do complete; the timeout is a bound (not a verdict). Recommended fix: after a spawn timeout, re-fetch the child's state and classify.

# Size audit concurrency ceiling to real proxy slot capacity

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an implementation agent or release producer, I want the audit runner's parallel-call
ceiling to match the proxy's real slot capacity, so calls do not queue behind slots and
inflate their own timeout budget into avoidable 600 s / 1,800 s caps.

## Problem statement

`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` defaults to 6 (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) while
`GET /llama/local/status` reports `total_slots: 2`, `available_slots: 0`. Six concurrent
`pi` sessions queue behind two slots; queue wait is charged against each call's timeout,
inflating p90 and pushing calls onto their budget (96 calls at 600 s, 13 at 1,800 s).
Slot-status querying already exists (`skill/audit/scripts/scan.py`) but is only used for
the *child* ceiling.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC3 (parent):** The audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from live slot status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor of 1, never exceeding reported capacity.
- **AC3 (parent):** When the slot query fails or times out, the runner falls back to the configured static ceiling (current behaviour preserved).
- **AC3 (parent):** An explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` value remains authoritative — it is never silently overridden by slot discovery.
- **AC3 (parent):** Unit tests prove all three behaviours: 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit env var ⇒ that exact value.
- The ceiling derivation is logged once per run (slot status, derived ceiling, source) so the decision is observable in the audit log.
- Full `skill/audit/tests/` suite passes.
- **Parent AC3 traceability:** the audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from the live slot status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor, never exceeding that capacity, falling back to the static ceiling when the query fails; unit tests prove 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` remains authoritative.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write the failing concurrency tests first in
   `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` (mock slot status).
2. Add a `_resolve_audit_ceiling()` helper in `audit_runner.py` that queries slot status
   (reusing the existing `scan.py` query), clamps by floor 1 and `total_slots`, and
   honours an explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`.
3. Route every ceiling consumer through the helper (parent and child paths).
4. Log the derivation once per run; update the constant docstring in
   `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` to describe the derivation rather than a bare 6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — ceiling resolution and consumers
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — existing slot-status query to reuse
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — ceiling default documentation
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — new tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — ceiling behaviour section

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the measurement harness + baseline child (SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG child 1):
  the change must be measured before/after with the committed harness.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (contention):** a slot-derived ceiling could still contend with interactive
  sessions. Mitigated by the floor of 1 and never exceeding `available_slots`.
- **Assumption:** `available_slots` is a trustworthy signal for admission; the fallback
  path keeps the runner functional when it is not.
- **Constraint:** do not raise timeouts to compensate — this change reduces queueing,
  not the budget.
data.title: Size audit concurrency ceiling to real proxy slot capacity

# Eliminate JSON-contract re-asks

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an implementation agent, I want a well-formed model response to be accepted on the
first call, so audit wall-clock is not spent re-asking — and the re-ask itself (p50
461 s, slower than the call it retries) is not billed twice.

## Problem statement

121 `verdict_reask` calls cost 18.7 h (13 % of all measured call time) and exist only
because the first response was not parseable JSON. `_reask_json_array_once` is the
fallback path; parse robustness is not hardened, so genuine-but-unusual formatting
(fenced blocks, prose prefix, trailing commas) triggers a full second call.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC4 (parent):** Parse robustness is hardened — a strict schema instruction is added to the prompt, tolerant extraction handles fenced ```json blocks and prose-prefixed JSON, and a single retry is attempted **only** on genuine failures (no parseable array found, or failed schema validation).
- **AC4 (parent):** A regression test proves a well-formed model response is never re-asked (the retry path is not invoked when the first response parses).
- **AC4 (parent):** Additional regression tests cover fenced blocks, prose-prefixed JSON, and trailing-comma tolerance — each accepted without a re-ask.
- **AC4 (parent):** A re-measurement on the same corpus shows `verdict_reask` at ≤ 2 % of all calls (currently ~7.4 %), recorded in the baseline document's successor report.
- Verdict semantics are unchanged: no response that would previously have been re-asked and then rejected may now be silently accepted with different semantics; the `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` vocabulary and the ready-to-close gate are frozen.
- Full `skill/audit/tests/` suite passes.
- **Parent AC4 traceability:** parse robustness is hardened (strict schema instruction, tolerant extraction, single retry only on genuine failures) and a regression test proves a well-formed model response is never re-asked; measured `verdict_reask` count drops to ≤ 2% of calls in a re-measurement on the same corpus.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write the failing tests first in
   `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py`: well-formed ⇒ no re-ask;
   fenced ⇒ parsed; prose-prefixed ⇒ parsed; trailing comma ⇒ parsed; genuinely
   unparseable ⇒ exactly one re-ask.
2. Harden `_extract_json_array` (tolerant extraction) and add an explicit JSON-schema
   instruction to the Phase 1 prompt template.
3. Gate `_reask_json_array_once` on genuine failure only; count re-asks in the
   `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY`.
4. Re-run the measurement harness and record the re-ask share.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — prompt template, `_extract_json_array`,
  `_reask_json_array_once`, reliability summary
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` — new tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — JSON contract section
- `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — re-measurement record

- Blocked by the measurement harness + baseline child (child 1) — the ≤ 2 % claim must
  be measured with the committed harness.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (correctness):** tolerant parsing could accept malformed verdicts. Mitigated by
  schema validation after extraction and by keeping the retry for genuine failures.
- **Constraint:** verdict semantics are frozen (parent brief §Constraints).

# Fingerprint from item data only, v2 line

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As an audit operator, I want the audit content fingerprint computed from this work item's own data only, with zero git calls, so an unrelated commit — or even a change to a file this item touched — never invalidates a stored audit.

**Producer decision (2026-10-21, comment SA-C0MVIAGIQU003WW4P):** option (a) — the strict item-data-only formula (title + description, zero git calls) supersedes the per-touched-path formula from SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P. This is the core slice of the parent item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` hashes a canonical JSON payload of **exactly** `{"schema": 2, "title_hash": <sha256(title)>, "description_hash": <sha256(description)>}` (`sort_keys=True`, then sha256 hex of the serialised payload). No `path_states`, no `key_files`, no comment-derived input (the Key Files section is part of the description and therefore already covered by `description_hash`).
2. The computation performs **zero git invocations**: it does not call `_resolve_touched_files`, `_compute_path_fingerprints` or any `git` subprocess, and is correspondingly fast (no repo probing) — asserted by a test that patches the git-executing helpers to raise.
3. `_compute_content_fingerprint` returns `None` (fail open → full re-audit) only when the work item cannot be fetched (`wl show` failure) or the payload cannot be built; a missing/garbage description still yields a deterministic hash.
4. `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` becomes the **versioned** `"Audit content fingerprint (v2): "`; `_extract_content_fingerprint` returns a value only for `v2` lines and returns `None` for unversioned legacy lines, so legacy reports fall through to the existing time-gate floor (`AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS` + persist-write tolerance) with **no silent mass re-audit wave**. All three persist sites (~5714, ~5740, ~6158) emit the versioned line.
5. The now-unused `comments` parameter of `_compute_content_fingerprint` is removed and every call site updated: `_check_audit_freshness` (~2020), `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~6606), `_run_remediation_loop` (~10171), `_phase_fetch_and_cq` (~10357), `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children` (~10786), `_phase_children` (~11516, ~11918). `cmd_check_freshness` (~2117/2120) keeps working and reports `hasFingerprint` from the versioned line.
6. **TDD, same commit:** the per-touched-path and comment-contribution invalidation tests are rewritten to assert the new rule *before* the behaviour change, and the change lands only when `skill/audit/tests` is green — the repo gate forbids a red commit, so code + test migration are one commit (`<WIP-id>: <summary>` recorded on this item).
7. Docstrings on `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_check_audit_freshness`, `_extract_content_fingerprint` and `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` describe the item-data-only, zero-git, versioned-line contract; no docstring still claims path/worktree/comment components.
8. Verdict semantics unchanged: `--force` still bypasses the gate; the freshness skip still returns the stored `rawOutput` verbatim (an explicit `Ready to close: No` is never masked).

## Minimal implementation

- Rewrite `_compute_content_fingerprint` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` to the item-data-only payload; drop the `comments` parameter and its plumbing.
- Version the prefix constant and make `_extract_content_fingerprint` version-aware (v2 only; legacy → `None`).
- Migrate the affected tests in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py`, `test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `test_no_breakage_chore.py`, `test_audit_runner_remediation.py` (literal-prefix assertions → the v2 constant).
- Keep `_resolve_touched_files` untouched (still used by the Phase-2 file-scope manifest at ~5257/~7964/~10897); dead-code removal is a separate item.

## Constraints

- Read-only: no test-suite execution or `pi` calls from the fingerprint path.
- Do not re-design the consumers (child reuse, read-only probe, ship `isAuditFresh`) — they must keep working against the simplified formula, not be extended.
- Documented trade-off (accepted): a stored audit may reference code that later changed, including files this item touched. The audit verdict remains the record for the item's own data.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, `_extract_content_fingerprint`, `_check_audit_freshness`, persist sites, call sites
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — rule migration
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` — probe expectations
- `skill/audit/tests/test_no_breakage_chore.py` — literal prefix assertions
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_remediation.py` — literal prefix assertion

# Ship gates accept versioned fingerprint line

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As a release operator, I want the ship audit gates to recognise the new versioned content-fingerprint line, so the content-freshness fast path keeps working after the fingerprint is versioned.

**Context:** `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` mirrors the runner's prefix (`AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = 'Audit content fingerprint: '`) and detects fingerprint-bearing audits with `haystack.includes(...)` (~line 478) to decide whether to spawn the read-only `check-freshness` probe (`queryContentFreshness`, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI). 1. `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` in `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` is updated to the versioned `'Audit content fingerprint (v2): '` (or `hasContentFingerprint` is made version-aware), so a v2-bearing audit is detected and the probe path is taken.

5. Sequencing note recorded: this item should land in the same release as the fingerprint change; if it lands later, the intervening window is fail-safe (extra re-audits, no incorrect passes).

- Extend `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` with the three cases.
